item.title: Swift Date Calculations: Calculating Time Differences Between Two Dates
item.description:
“Swift Date Calculations: Calculating Time Differences Between Two Dates”

How does one effectively calculate the precise time interval, formatted or raw, between two Date objects in Swift? Developers often need to derive differences in years, months, days, hours, minutes, or seconds. Several robust methods exist, leveraging the Calendar class, DateComponentsFormatter, or custom Date extensions.

This exploration details multiple accepted solutions suitable for different Swift environments and output requirements, from simple numerical components to fully localized strings.

item.title: Java Date & Time: Obtaining UTC Values
item.description:
“Java Date & Time: Obtaining UTC Values”

Java’s handling of dates and times, particularly with older classes like java.util.Date and java.util.Calendar, can be a source of confusion. The core issue is that java.util.Date objects themselves don’t intrinsically hold time zone information; their string representations often default to the JVM’s current time zone, leading to misunderstandings.

This post delves into the most effective methods for obtaining accurate UTC (Coordinated Universal Time) values in Java, steering clear of the pitfalls associated with legacy APIs. We will explore modern approaches and provide practical code examples.

item.title: PHP: Convert Timestamps to Human-Readable 'Time Ago' Format
item.description:
“PHP: Convert Timestamps to Human-Readable ‘Time Ago’ Format”

When displaying a timestamp of a past event, it’s often more user-friendly to show how long ago it occurred (e.g., “2 minutes ago,” “3 hours ago,” “1 week ago”) rather than the raw date and time. This practice is common on social media platforms and news sites to provide context. PHP offers several ways to achieve this, ranging from simple manual calculations to using established libraries.
